name: Chennai extreme rainfall 2015
evidence_notes: IMD/IMS report records 490 mm at Tambaram in 24 hours beginning 1 December 2015 and flooding across Chennai, Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur, and Cuddalore.
feature_method: IMD station maximum reported for the stated 24-hour period; duration is the 3-day documented event window. Antecedent features omitted until derived from a gridded or district rainfall time series.
cyclone_window_evidence: Screened the event plus two-day buffer against IMD cyclone-season records; no named cyclone landfall is recorded in the buffered 28 November–4 December window. The source describes the event as rainfall-driven flooding.

name: Southern Tamil Nadu extreme rainfall 2023
evidence_notes: IMD report records 95 cm at Kayalpattinam on 18 December 2023 and extreme rainfall across Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli, Kanyakumari, and Tenkasi during 17–19 December.
feature_method: IMD station maximum reported for 18 December; duration is the 3-day documented event window. Antecedent features omitted until derived from a gridded or district rainfall time series.
cyclone_window_evidence: Screened the event plus two-day buffer (15–21 December 2023) against IMD cyclone records; Cyclone Michaung's early-December landfall is outside this window, and no named cyclone landfall is recorded during the southern rainfall event.

name: Mayiladuthurai–Cuddalore extreme rainfall 2022
evidence_notes: IMD report records 44 cm at Sirkazhi, 32 cm at Kollidam, 31 cm at Chidambaram, and inland flooding in Mayiladuthurai, Cuddalore, Tiruvallur, and adjoining districts during 12–14 November.
feature_method: IMD station maximum reported for 12 November; duration is the 5-day documented event window. Antecedent features omitted until derived from a gridded or district rainfall time series.
cyclone_window_evidence: Screened the event plus two-day buffer (10–18 November 2022) against the IMD seasonal report and cyclone records. The report describes a low-pressure system, not a named cyclone landfall, during this event.

name: North coastal Tamil Nadu heavy rainfall 2022
evidence_notes: IMD report lists heavy rainfall across Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Mayiladuthurai, and Cuddalore during 1–4 November 2022.
feature_method: IMD maximum daily station rainfall within the 1-4 November event; duration is the 4-day documented event window. Antecedent features omitted until derived from a gridded or district rainfall time series.
cyclone_window_evidence: Screened the event plus two-day buffer (30 October–6 November 2022) against the IMD seasonal report and cyclone records; no named cyclone landfall is recorded in this window.

name: North Tamil Nadu depression rainfall 2024
evidence_notes: IMD report describes the 15–17 October 2024 Bay of Bengal depression and heavy rainfall in Chennai and Tiruvallur, including 23 cm at Kathivakkam and 21 cm at Manali on 16 October.
feature_method: IMD station maximum of 30 cm reported for the 24-hour period; duration is the 3-day documented event window. Antecedent features omitted until derived from a gridded or district rainfall time series.
cyclone_window_evidence: Screened the event plus two-day buffer (13–19 October 2024) against the IMD seasonal report and cyclone records. The report identifies a depression during the event, with no named cyclone landfall in the buffered window.

name: Kanyakumari extreme rainfall and flooding 2021
evidence_notes: IMD records recurrent heavy rainfall over Kanyakumari during 12–15 November, 50–55 cm cumulative at Perunchani and Puthan dams and 25–35 cm across the rest of the district, causing reservoir overflow and extensive flooding. The maximum reported 24-hour station rainfall was 22 cm on 14 November.
feature_method: IMD station maximum of 22 cm on 14 November (converted to 220 mm); duration is the four-day documented rainfall and flood period. Antecedent features are derived separately from the district gridded rainfall series.
cyclone_window_evidence: The IMD seasonal report identifies an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the southeast Arabian Sea and a separate Bay of Bengal depression, but no named cyclone landfall during 10–17 November 2021. The event is classified as rainfall-driven; the project exclusion is named-cyclone landfall, not non-cyclonic depressions or upper-air circulations.

name: Chennai extreme rainfall and flooding 2021
evidence_notes: IMD records 24 cm at DGP Office in Chennai and very-heavy to extremely-heavy rainfall reports across Chennai and adjoining Tiruvallur in the 24 hours ending 08:30 IST on 31 December. The report describes the event as a trough-driven mesoscale episode and reports extensive inland flooding and traffic blocks in Chennai and neighbourhood.
feature_method: IMD station maximum of 24 cm during the 24-hour reporting period ending 31 December (converted to 240 mm); duration is the reported 24-hour event period. District-average grid features are derived separately.
cyclone_window_evidence: Screened 28 December 2021–2 January 2022 against the IMD seasonal report and cyclone records. The event is attributed to troughs; Cyclonic Storm Jawad's 2–6 December track is outside the buffered window, and no named cyclone landfall is recorded in it.

name: Tamil Nadu multi-region extreme rainfall and flooding 2024
evidence_notes: IMD reports 54 cm at Oothu (Tirunelveli) on 13 December and extreme rainfall reports in the listed southern, delta, and adjoining districts. The report states that overflowing rivers and dam releases caused severe flooding and low-lying inundation across South Tamil Nadu, the delta and adjoining districts, and Chennai and adjoining districts. District labels are the report's named extreme-rain districts within those impact regions; they are not flood polygons.
feature_method: IMD station maximum of 54 cm at Oothu on 13 December (converted to 540 mm); duration is the three-day documented extreme-rainfall and flooding period. District-average grid features are derived separately.
cyclone_window_evidence: Screened 10–16 December 2024 against the IMD seasonal report and cyclone records. The report attributes the rainfall to a well-marked low-pressure area; Cyclone Fengal's 30 November landfall is outside this buffered event window, and no named cyclone landfall is recorded in it.

name: Nilgiris extreme rainfall and flooding 2019
evidence_notes: The Central Water Commission's 9 August 2019 flood situation report records 91 cm at Avalanche in Nilgiris, reports the Bhavani rising rapidly after the rainfall, and lists Nilgiris and Coimbatore among flood-affected districts. District labels represent the report's affected-district list, not mapped inundation polygons.
feature_method: Maximum point-station rainfall at Avalanche, reported by the CWC as 91 cm on 9 August (converted to 910 mm); 96 hours is the fixed 6–9 August event-window length, not a measured continuous rainfall duration. Supplementary district-average daily grid features are stored separately.
cyclone_window_evidence: The IMD Annual Report 2019 identifies a deep depression during 6–9 August, but no named cyclone landfall occurs in the 4–11 August event-plus-buffer window. The event is retained under the project's named-cyclone-landfall exclusion and explicitly recorded as depression-associated rainfall; it is not represented as a cyclone-free synoptic event.

name: North Tamil Nadu heavy-rain inundation 2021
evidence_notes: NRSC/ISRO's ALOS-2 PALSAR rapid map records inundation in five districts, with visible inundation in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Villupuram, and Cuddalore on 8 November 2021. The map itself cautions that this is preliminary, ungrounded-verified mapping and may include rainwater accumulation in low-lying areas; labels denote mapped district intersections, not district-wide flooding.
feature_method: Intensity is the maximum district-mean daily total (91.5 mm in Nagapattinam on 3 November) from the project's IMD 0.25-degree gridded rainfall series over the 1–8 November window; it is not a point-station extreme. Duration is the eight-day analysis-window length, not measured continuous rain. District-wise daily maxima and antecedent totals are stored separately in event_district_features.json.
cyclone_window_evidence: The event window is 1–8 November with a fixed two-day buffer (30 October–10 November). The NRSC map attributes the episode to Northeast Monsoon rain. IMD's 6 November release describes low-pressure areas; the Bay depression and later North Tamil Nadu coastal crossing occurred after this buffer (18–19 November). No named cyclone landfall is recorded in the event-plus-buffer window.

name: Kanyakumari heavy rain and flooding, December 2010
evidence_notes: IMD's 2010 annual report attributes heavy to very heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu during 6–8 December to a depression over the Bay of Bengal. It specifically reports 4,500 huts damaged and about 1,000 acres of paddy fields submerged in Kanyakumari district. The district observatory's IMD December extremes table records a 24-hour maximum of 62.9 mm on 9 December; this is a point-observatory measurement, not a district mean.
feature_method: Intensity is the Kanyakumari IMD observatory's 24-hour maximum of 62.9 mm dated 9 December 2010 in the official December extremes table. The four-day duration is the inclusive 6–9 December analysis-window length, not measured continuous rainfall. The impact label is taken from the IMD annual report; station rainfall and district impact labels are distinct evidence types.
cyclone_window_evidence: The fixed two-day buffer spans 4–11 December 2010. The IMD annual report's storm chronology identifies the associated 7–8 December system as a depression; its named Severe Cyclonic Storm Jal occurred 4–8 November, outside this window. No named cyclone landfall is recorded for the event-plus-buffer window. This remains a depression-associated event, not a system-free rainfall case.
